catalog.summary: Vertical list of items with sections.

patternAbsent.reason: The Authoring Practices publish no pattern for a static list. They name Listbox and Grid for interactive collections and nothing between those and plain content, so the governing sources are the platform and the roles model.

rootRole.reason: The row is a two-column layout of a content box and its independent targets, and CSS has no `display` that is both `list-item` and a grid, so the family draws its own marker and the native one is always gone. Safari and VoiceOver drop list semantics whenever CSS removes the marker, and the article's own answer is `role="list"` on the element. Writing it always is therefore a consequence of the layout rather than a habit: MUI never writes it and loses the semantics in Safari, Angular Material writes it without saying why.

wiring.aria-busy: true on the root while the list is loading, which ARIA 1.2 section 5.2.6 requires of a container whose required owned elements have not arrived
wiring.aria-label: the consumer's own name for the set, forwarded from `label`
wiring.aria-labelledby: forwarded from `labelledBy`; a section's heading names its own nested list this way
wiring.role: list, on the root and on every section's nested list, because the family draws its own marker and the native one is gone

keyboard.effect: moves to the next focusable element; every control a row holds is in the page tab sequence
moves to the previous focusable element, under the same rule

keyboardDeparture.reason: Fluent, React Aria and Angular Material each bind arrows over a list, and each first changes the role to one that permits them. `docs/component-features.md` section 10 refuses `role="list"` with an invented keyboard, so the collection keyboard is deferred to `listbox` and `table` in wave 6 rather than written here under a role that cannot carry it.
keyboardDeparture.cost: A reader tabbing through a hundred rows presses Tab a hundred times. That is the platform's behaviour for any page of links; a labelled `nav` around the list is what a screen reader jumps by instead.

selection.reason: ARIA 1.2 does not allow `aria-selected` on `listitem`, so a selection model here would announce nothing. The row still paints a selection the page owns through `data-selected`, and the control that announces it is a `checkbox` composed into the row's `start`.

virtualization.reason: `docs/process/build-order.md` retires `virtual-list` as a family and makes windowing a capability of the collection engine, whose first consumer is `listbox`.

orientation.reason: A list that flows sideways is `<Inline>` around the same rows, and `inline` already answers gap, alignment and wrapping: `<Inline gap="4">{rows}</Inline>`.

landmark.reason: A landmark is a page-structure decision the page owns, and `breadcrumb` already holds the one case where the family is the navigation. One line composes it: `<nav aria-label="Sections"><List>…</List></nav>`.

section.reason: A group inside a list is an `li` holding a heading and a nested list, which is the grouping HTML already has. MUI, Angular Material, Primer and React Aria each place the heading loose among the rows instead, so a reader hears a heading inside a set rather than a set with a name.

sticky.reason: MUI's `ListSubheader` is sticky unless it is told not to be. Composing it needs the family's own surface token and stack level; a consumer writing `position: sticky` alone gets a heading with rows showing through it.

empty.reason: A message placed outside the `ul` is outside the box the family paints, and the reader hears "list, 0 items" and then nothing. Inside, the reader hears the message. The family supplies the box and the row height; `result-state` supplies the words.

marker.number: a CSS counter the set resets and the row increments
marker.reason: A character is never an icon — `docs/token-foundation.md` rule 3 — so the bullet is the library's own dot geometry rather than a `•` in a `content` string. The counter is the one name the two families share; no selector in either stylesheet reaches the other's `data-ui`, which is the rule `accordion` and `collapsible` set.

sectionLabel.caption: The small muted name of the group.
sectionLabel.ruled: The name in the text colour over a rule, with no ground behind it.
sectionLabel.end: What stands at the end of the heading on the line of the name, a day balance or a count, in tabular figures. React takes it as the end prop of ListSection; Angular marks an element of the heading with slListSectionEnd.
